                                                                                      SST39SF010A/
                                            SST39SF020A/SST39SF040

              1-Mbit/2-Mbit/4-Mbit (x8) Multi-Purpose Flash


Features                                                                Product Description

•  Organized as 128K x 8/256K x 8/512K x 8                              The SST39SF010A/020A/040 devices are CMOS
•  Single 4.5V-5.5V Read and Write Operations                           Multi-Purpose Flash (MPF) manufactured with
•  Superior Reliability:                                                Microchip’s proprietary, high-performance CMOS
  -  Endurance: 100,000 Cycles (typical)                                SuperFlash® technology. The split-gate cell design and
  -  Greater than 100 years data retention                              thick oxide tunneling injector attain better reliability and
                                                                        manufacturability compared with alternate approaches.
•  Low-Power Consumption (typical values at                             The SST39SF010A/020A/040 devices write (Program
  14 MHz):                                                              or Erase) with a 4.5V-5.5V power supply and conform
  -  Active current: 10 mA (typical)                                    to JEDEC® standard pin assignments for x8 memories.
  -  Standby current: 30 µA (typical)                                   Featuring a high-performance Byte Program, the
•  Sector Erase Capability:                                             SST39SF010A/020A/040 devices provide a maximum
  -  Uniform 4-Kbyte sectors                                            Byte Program time of 20µsec. These devices use
•  Fast Read Access Time:                                               Toggle Bit or Data# Polling to indicate the completion of
  -  55 ns                                                              Program operation. To protect against inadvertent
                                                                        writes, they have on-chip hardware and software data
  -  70 ns                                                              protection schemes.
•   Latched Address and Data                                            The SST39SF010A/020A/040 devices provide
•  Automatic Write Timing:                                              superior reliability, being designed, manufactured and
  -  Internal VPP Generation                                            tested for a wide spectrum of applications.
•  Fast Erase and Byte Program:                                         These devices are suited for applications that require
  -  Sector Erase time: 18 ms (typical)                                 convenient and economical updating of program,
  -  Chip Erase time: 70 ms (typical)                                   configuration or data memory. For all system
  -  Byte Program time: 14 µs (typical)                                 applications, they significantly improve performance
  -  Chip Rewrite time:                                                 and reliability while lowering power consumption. They
     -  2 seconds (typical) for SST39SF010A                             inherently use less energy during Erase and Program
                                                                        times than alternative Flash technologies. The total
     -  4 seconds (typical) for SST39SF020A                             energy consumed is a function of the applied voltage,
     -  8 seconds (typical) for SST39SF040                              current and time of application. Since, for any given
•  End-of-Write Detection:                                              voltage range, the SuperFlash technology uses less
  -  Toggle Bit                                                         current to program and has a shorter erase time, the
  -  Data# Polling                                                      total energy consumed during any Erase or Program
                                                                        operation is less than alternative Flash technologies.
•  TTL I/O Compatibility                                                These devices also improve flexibility while lowering
•  JEDEC® Standard:                                                     the cost for program, data and configuration storage
  -  Flash EEPROM pinouts and command sets                              applications.
•  All Devices are RoHS Compliant                                       The SuperFlash technology provides fixed Erase and
                                                                        Program times, independent of the number of
Packages                                                                Erase/Program cycles that have occurred. Therefore,
•  32-Pin PDIP, 32-Lead PLCC and 32-Lead TSOP                           the system software or hardware does not have to be
                                                                        modified or derated as is necessary with alternative
                                                                        Flash technologies, whose Erase and Program times
                                                                        increase with accumulated Erase/Program cycles.
                                                                        See Figure 2-1 for pin assignments and Table 2-1 for
                                                                        pin descriptions.

TABLE 2-1:       PIN DESCRIPTION
   Symbol            Pin Name                                                                   Functions

AMS(1)-A0     Address Inputs       Provide memory addresses. During Sector Erase AMS-A12 address lines will select the sector.

                                         Output data during Read cycles and receive input data during Write cycles.
DQ7-DQ0     Data Input/Output            Data are internally latched during a Write cycle.
                                         The outputs are in tri-state when OE# or CE# is high.
CE#              Chip Enable            Activate the device when CE# is low.
OE#              Output Enable        Gate the data output buffers.
WE#             Write Enable           Control the Write operations.
VDD              Power Supply         Provide power supply voltage: 4.5V-5.5V.
VSS               Ground
NC                No Connection        Unconnected pins.
Note  1:    AMS = Most significant address
              AMS = A16 for SST39SF010A, A17 for SST39SF020A and A18 for SST39SF040

operation will be ignored.                                               Polling or Toggle Bit maybe be read concurrently with
                                                                         the completion of the write cycle. If this occurs, the
                                                                         system may receive incorrect results from the status
                                                                         detection process. For example, valid data may appear
                                                                         to conflict with either DQ7 or DQ6. To prevent false
                                                                         results upon detection of failures, the software routine
                                                                         should loop to read the accessed location an additional
                                                                         two times. If both reads are valid, then the device has
                                                                         completed the Write cycle; otherwise the failure is valid.

3.12     Product Identification Mode
         Exit/Reset
To return to the standard Read mode, the Software
Product Identification mode must be exited. Exit is
accomplished by issuing the Exit ID command
sequence, which returns the device to the Read
operation. Please note that the software reset
command is ignored during an internal Program or
Erase operation. See Ta b l e  4 - 2 for the software
command codes, Figure 7-9 for the timing waveform
and Figure 7-14 for a flowchart.

Absolute Maximum Ratings (†)
Temperature under bias ..........................................................................................................................-55°C to +125°C
Storage temperature ...............................................................................................................................-65°C to +150°C
DC voltage on any pin to ground potential...........................................................................................-0.5V to VDD+0.5V
Transient voltage (<20 ns) on any pin to ground potential...................................................................-2.0V to VDD+2.0V
Voltage on A9 pin to ground potential  ....................................................................................................... -0.5V to 13.2V
Package power dissipation capability (TA = +25°C).....................................................................................................1W
Through hold lead soldering temperature (10 seconds) ....................................................................................... +300°C
Surface mount lead soldering temperature (3 seconds) ....................................................................................... +240°C
Output short circuit current(1) ................................................................................................................................100 mA
 † NOTICE: Stresses above those listed under “Absolute Maximum Ratings” may cause permanent damage to the
 device. This is a stress rating only, and functional operation of the device at those or any other conditions above those
 indicated in the operational listings of this specification is not implied. Exposure to maximum rating conditions for
 extended periods may affect device reliability.


    Note 1:   Output shorted for no more than one second. No more than one output shorted at a time.

 TCS             WE# and CE# Setup Time                                                                                  0                 —              ns
 TCH            WE# and CE# Hold Time                                                                                    0                 —              ns
 TOES          OE# High Setup Time                                                                                       0                 —              ns
 TOEH          OE# High Hold Time                                                                                        10                —              ns
 TCP            CE# Pulse Width                                                                                              40                —              ns
 TWP            WE# Pulse Width                                                                                             40                —              ns
 TWPH(1)      WE# Pulse Width High                                                                                     30                —              ns
 TCPH(1)       CE# Pulse Width High                                                                                     30                —              ns
 TDS            Data Setup Time                                                                                              40                —              ns
 TDH(1)         Data Hold Time                                                                                                 0                 —              ns
 TIDA(1)        Software ID, Bypass Entry and Exit Times                                                       —               150            ns
 TSE             Sector Erase                                                                                                      —                25             ms
 TSCE           Chip Erase                                                                                                         —               100            ms
 Note  1:    This parameter is measured only for initial qualification and after a design or process change that could
                  affect this parameter.

                                                                 Document status changed from “Preliminary
Revision F (May 2025)                                            Specification” to “Data Sheet”; Changed IDD Program
Corrected pin assignments for 32-Lead PLCC;                      and Erase maximum values from 25 to 35 in Table 7 on
Updated 32-Lead TSOP package marking.                            page 12.

Revision E (November 2024)                                       Revision 03 (March 2003)

Updated Package Marking section.                                 Changes to Table 7 on page 12; Added footnote for
                                                                 MPF power usage and Typical conditions; Clarified the
Revision D (September 2024)                                      Test Conditions for Power Supply Current and Read
                                                                 parameters; Clarified IDD Write to be Program and
Replaced WHE package type with TU package type.                  Erase.

Revision C (April 2016)                                          Revision 02 (May 2002)
Corrected typo in “Product Ordering Information”                 2002 Data Book
section.

Revision B (April 2013)

End of Life for all 45 ns valid combinations; Updated
Table 6 and Table 11.

Revision A (July 2011)
All 45ns parts reinstated; Applied new document
format; Released document under letter revision
system; Updated spec number from S71147 to
DS25022.

Revision 09 (January 2010)
End of Life for all 45ns valid combinations. See
S71147(02); Added replacement 55ns valid
combinations.

Revision 08 (September 2009)

Changed endurance from 10,000 to 100,000 in
“Product Description” section.

Revision 07 (March 2009)
Removed leaded parts from valid combinations. See
PSN-D0PB0001.

Revision 06 (August 2004)
Corrected Revision History for Version 04: IDD
maximum value was incorrectly stated as 30mA
instead of 35 mA.

Revision 05 (November 2003)
2004 Data Book; Added non-Pb MPNs and removed
footnote.

PRODUCT IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM

To order or obtain information, e.g., on pricing or delivery, refer to the factory or the listed sales office.

                                      SST   39 SF 010A - 70 - 4C - NHE - T
                                               XX  XX XXXX   XX   XX     XXX  - X---


                                                                                            Shipping Carrier Option
                                                                                            Blank = Standard Packaging (tube or tray)
                                                                                            T = Tape and Reel



                Product Series                                                          Package Type
        39 = Multi-Purpose Flash                                                        PHE = PDIP, 32-Pins or Leads, non-Pb
                                                                                        NHE = PLCC, 32-Pins or Leads, non-Pb
                                                                                        TU = TSOP, 32-Pins or Leads, non-Pb


                     Voltage
               S = 4.5V-5.5V                                                         Temperature Range
                                                                                     C = Commercial = 0°C to +70°C
                                                                                     I = Industrial = -40°C to +85°C

                              Device Density
                                 040 = 4 Mbit                                 Minimum Endurance
                                 020 = 2 Mbit                                 4 = 10,000 cycles
                                 010 = 1 Mbit


                                           Version                        Read Access Speed
                           A = Version Letter                             55 = 55 ns
                                                                          70 = 70 ns

Microchip Devices Code Protection Feature

Note the following details of the code protection feature on Microchip products:
•  Microchip products meet the specifications contained in their particular Microchip Data Sheet.
•  Microchip believes that its family of products is secure when used in the intended manner, within operating
  specifications, and under normal conditions.
•  Microchip values and aggressively protects its intellectual property rights. Attempts to breach the code protection
  features of Microchip product is strictly prohibited and may violate the Digital Millennium Copyright Act.
•  Neither Microchip nor any other semiconductor manufacturer can guarantee the security of its code. Code
  protection does not mean that we are guaranteeing the product is “unbreakable”. Code protection is constantly
  evolving. Microchip is committed to continuously improving the code protection features of our products.
